name: Passo dello Stelvio
description: The east side climbs out of the Vinschgau valley past Gomagoi and Trafoi, then stacks 48 numbered hairpins up a bare wall below the Ortler glaciers to 2,758 m, one of the highest paved passes in the Alps. The Giro has crossed it many times, usually as its highest point of the race, and Fausto Coppi's 1953 attack here is part of Giro legend.
famousFor: 48 numbered hairpins on the Prato side; Giro's highest point (Cima Coppi); Coppi 1953
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme published max (steepest profile segment average, not a 100 m peak)

name: Alpe d'Huez
description: From the Romanche valley floor the road kicks straight into its steepest ramps and then winds through 21 numbered hairpins, each signed with the names of past stage winners, to the ski resort. It is the Tour de France's most famous summit finish, with huge roadside crowds, including the Dutch corner at hairpin 7.
famousFor: 21 numbered hairpins; the Tour de France summit finish
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme published max (steepest profile segment); first 3 km after the valley are the steepest part

name: Mont Ventoux
description: After an easy start through vineyards, the road turns sharp left at Saint-Estève into a long forest section at around 9-10 %, then breaks out at Chalet Reynard onto the white, treeless scree slopes to the weather station at the top. The 'Giant of Provence' is famous for wind and heat, and for the memorial to Tom Simpson, who died near the summit during the 1967 Tour.
famousFor: Giant of Provence; lunar summit; Tom Simpson memorial
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme published max (steepest profile segment)

name: Col du Tourmalet
description: The western side climbs from Luz through the Gorge de Barèges and the village of Barèges, then up open high pasture to the 2,115 m pass. The Tourmalet is the most-crossed mountain in Tour de France history, first raced in 1910, and the 2010 Tour finished on its summit.
famousFor: Most-climbed pass in Tour de France history (first in 1910)
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme published max (steepest profile segment)

name: Col du Galibier
description: The ride follows the D 902 from the centre of Valloire, along the Valloirette past Plan Lachat, and up the open road to the 2,642 m summit. The tunnel below the last kilometre is closed to bicycles. Raced by the Tour since 1911, it is where Marco Pantani made his decisive 1998 attack, and it is usually ridden straight after the Col du Télégraphe.
famousFor: Tour de France high point since 1911; Pantani 1998; paired with the Télégraphe
maxGradeNote: max from cols-cyclisme Saint-Michel profile segment (Les Granges du Galibier); not a 100 m peak

name: Passo del Mortirolo
description: A narrow, wooded road that leaves the Valtellina at Mazzo and stays above 10 % for most of its length with almost no rest, only easing in the last 3 km to the pass at 1,852 m. It is the side where Marco Pantani launched his famous 1994 Giro attack, and a monument to him stands on the climb.
famousFor: One of the hardest climbs in Europe; Pantani 1994
maxGradeNote: steepest 500 m section in the source profile; peak ramps of ~18 % are widely quoted (official Giro text: "gradients of up to 18%")

name: Monte Zoncolan
description: From Ovaro the road rises gently through Liariis, then turns into a relentless wall averaging 13-16 % for 6 km through the forest, finishing through three short tunnels on the open summit at 1,730 m. The Giro has used it as one of its most brutal summit finishes, with huge crowds packed into the steep final kilometres.
famousFor: The Giro's most brutal summit finish
maxGradeNote: steepest profile segment (400 m); short pitches above 20 % are commonly quoted

name: Passo di Gavia
description: The south side climbs from Ponte di Legno past Sant'Apollonia, then narrows to a single-lane road with a tunnel high up and steep hairpins to the 2,621 m pass between glacial peaks. In the 1988 Giro, Andy Hampsten crossed it in a snowstorm and took the pink jersey, one of cycling's most famous days.
famousFor: Snowstorm stage of the 1988 Giro (Hampsten)
maxGradeNote: steepest profile segment in the salite.ch profile (km 7.5-8)

name: Passo Giau
description: The ride leaves Selva di Cadore on the SP 638. After the village the gradient barely leaves 8-10 %, through 29 numbered hairpins, three avalanche galleries and larch forest, past Rifugio Fedare, and onto the open meadows below Nuvolau and Ra Gusela at 2,236 m. It is a Giro favourite and a centrepiece of the Maratona dles Dolomites.
famousFor: 29 hairpins of steady 9-10 % in the heart of the Dolomites
maxGradeNote: steepest profile segment

name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo (Rifugio Auronzo)
description: From Lake Misurina the road rolls past Lago d'Antorno and the toll gate, dips slightly, then the last 4 km climb at 11-13 % straight up to Rifugio Auronzo at the foot of the three famous rock towers. The Giro has finished here several times, often in snow.
famousFor: Giro summit finish below the Three Peaks; brutal last 4 km
maxGradeNote: steepest 500 m segment

name: Alto de l'Angliru
description: The first 6 km from Riosa are a normal mountain road, then after a short flat the last 6.5 km never drop below 11 % and peak on the Cueña les Cabres ramp, on a narrow road with mist and cows. Since its Vuelta debut in 1999 it has been the race's most feared summit finish.
famousFor: The Vuelta's most feared summit; Cueña les Cabres 23.5 %
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme header; the Cueña les Cabres ramp ~3 km from the top is usually quoted at 23.5 % (cyclingstage)

name: Sa Calobra (Coll dels Reis)
description: A dead-end road built in the 1930s that snakes up from the tiny port through limestone cliffs, including the 270-degree 'knot' where the road loops under itself, to the Coll dels Reis. It is a classic winter and spring training test for pro teams and amateurs based on Mallorca.
famousFor: Corkscrew hairpins and the knot-tie loop; pro training test on Mallorca
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme header (steepest segment, last 400 m)

name: Col d'Izoard
description: After the Guil gorge the climb proper turns off towards Arvieux and Brunissard, steepens through larch forest, then dips into the Casse Déserte, a lunar landscape of scree and rock pinnacles, before the last ramp to 2,361 m. It is a Tour legend where Coppi and Bobet are honoured with a memorial, and the 2017 Tour finished on top.
famousFor: The Casse Déserte moonscape; Coppi and Bobet memorial
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme published max (short ramp after the Casse Déserte dip)

name: La Planche des Belles Filles
description: A short, steep Vosges climb out of Plancher-les-Mines through pine forest to the ski station, averaging over 8 % with a final kick at the top. It has been a Tour de France summit finish since 2012 and hosted the decisive 2020 time trial.
famousFor: Short, steep Tour summit finish in the Vosges (since 2012)
maxGradeNote: steepest 250 m segment in the paved profile (km 0.75-1.0); cols-cyclisme header lists 22 %, which refers to the gravel "Super Planche" extension above the station

name: Vršič
region: Upper Carniola (Julian Alps, Triglav National Park)
description: The ride starts on the way out of Kranjska Gora, about half a kilometre before Lake Jasna, and follows the road to the Pišnica bridge. From the bridge at 850 m Slovenia's highest road pass climbs past the Russian Chapel through 24 numbered hairpins, several of them cobbled, to 1,611 m under the walls of Prisojnik. The road was built during the First World War by Russian prisoners of war and is often called the Russian Road.
famousFor: Highest pass in Slovenia; 24 numbered hairpins on the north side; the Russian Road
maxGradeNote: steepest profile segment

name: Mangart Saddle road (Mangartsko sedlo)
side: Junction with the Predel road above Log pod Mangartom
description: The highest road in Slovenia leaves the Predel road at a bridge and climbs a narrow balcony road through five rock tunnels and across sheer cliffs to the saddle below Mangart (2,055 m) and a loop at the top. Views over the Julian Alps and into Italy make it one of the most spectacular climbs in the Alps.
famousFor: Highest road in Slovenia; five rock tunnels; Julian Alps views
maxGradeNote: steepest segment in this coarse (~0.9 km) profile; real short pitches are much steeper (climbfinder: steepest 100 m 18.8 %)

name: Krvavec
description: The Pogi Challenge climb: from the end of Grad, near Cerklje na Gorenjskem, the paved road climbs past Ambrož pod Krvavcem and Planina Jezerca to Plaža beside Hotel Krvavec. The first kilometres are the steepest, there is a short dip near km 3, then a hard run through Ambrož to Jezerca and a steeper finish across the pastures to 1,594 m. It is Tadej Pogačar's home climb and the finish of the Tour of Slovenia 2024 stage to Plaža.
famousFor: Pogačar's home climb; Pogi Challenge finish; Tour of Slovenia summit at Plaža
maxGradeNote: steepest half-kilometre on the CyclingCols Grad profile (km 1.2–1.7)

name: Großglockner High Alpine Road (Fuscher Törl)
description: From Fusch the road climbs gently to the Ferleiten toll gate, then settles into 10-11 % for 12 km up the Hohe Tauern toll road past Piffkar and Hexenküche to the Fuscher Törl at 2,394 m, facing Austria's highest peaks. It is a regular feature of the Tour of Austria and of big amateur hill climbs.
famousFor: Austria's great alpine toll road; 12 km at 10 %
maxGradeNote: steepest profile segment (below Edelweisswand)

name: Col de la Madeleine
description: The southern side leaves La Chambre on the D213 and climbs through Saint-Martin-sur-la-Chambre and the forest, then the resort of Saint-François-Longchamp and open pasture to the pass between the Maurienne and the Tarentaise. It is a regular Tour de France HC climb.
famousFor: Long, steady Tour HC climb between Maurienne and Tarentaise
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme published max (short ramp near l'Epalud)

name: Mur de Huy (Chemin des Chapelles)
description: A short, savage wall that leaves the town of Huy and climbs the Chemin des Chapelles past small roadside chapels, steepening in the middle before easing slightly at the line. It has been the finish of La Flèche Wallonne since 1983.
famousFor: Finish of La Flèche Wallonne
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme published max; the hairpin at the chapels is widely quoted at about 26 %

name: Lagos de Covadonga
side: Soto de Cangas (near Cangas de Onís)
description: After 5 km of valley road past the basilica of Covadonga, the climb rears up into the Picos de Europa, with the steep La Huesera section and the Mirador de la Reina, a short descent near the top and a final ramp to the glacial lakes Enol and Ercina. It has been the Vuelta's signature summit finish since 1983.
famousFor: The Vuelta's signature summit finish (since 1983)
maxGradeNote: steepest profile segment (La Huesera, km 11-12)

name: Puy de Dôme
side: Panoramique des Dômes toll road (lower station)
description: The final road spirals around the extinct volcano at a near-constant 12 %, with views over the Chaîne des Puys, to the summit at about 1,412 m. Normally closed to bikes and cars (a rack railway runs alongside), it is famous for the 1964 Tour shoulder-to-shoulder duel between Poulidor and Anquetil and returned to the Tour in 2023.
famousFor: Poulidor vs Anquetil 1964; volcano road reopened for the 2023 Tour
maxGradeNote: cols-cyclisme published max
